🔖 Forget short-term price charts – Washington’s digital asset framework is the legal authorization that conservative wealth managers have been waiting for before they can put trillions to work. Everyone seems to be watching the CLARITY Act for the same thing. From retail traders to institutional giants, people are waiting for the green light that confirms Washington has clarified the market. Legislation doesn’t move markets through a single, uniform mechanism. 

☄️ The GENIUS Act has limitations on a single-asset framework for payment stablecoins. CLARITY works at a different layer: a horizontal market-structure bill covering how digital assets are classified, who regulates them, and who is allowed to custody and trade them.

⁉️ That’s why its success shouldn’t be benchmarked against a single price chart. The metric that matters here is the slower signal underneath: custody mandates being written, treasury policies being rewritten, allocation committees granting their first approvals.

⚠️ That’s the real story. The CLARITY Act is fundamentally a legal permission structure. By handing institutional wealth managers and world-class operators the regulatory green light they need to enter the room, this law achieves something more durable than a market rally. It moves the people who build markets, not just the capital.

In an unprecedented move, French authorities accused the head of a major platform of crimes committed by its users.

That investigation is still ongoing, although it makes less sense with each passing year. 

Why?

Because we now have extensive evidence that Telegram was neither worse than other popular platforms at moderation, nor the worst at cooperating with authorities.

So why was Telegram singled out?

Over the last two years, we have seen a pattern emerge in multiple countries: Telegram is quietly pressured to grant political favors — such as illegal censorship or surveillance. When we refuse, local media and “non-governmental” organizations launch orchestrated campaigns portraying Telegram as a cesspool of crime, from child pornography to terrorism.

Our moderation is no worse than that of other major platforms. Yet these campaigns instill the idea that Telegram should be persecuted or restricted.

Suddenly, officials start caring about crime and protecting children — but only on platforms that reject their secret political demands. Platforms that accept such deals get away with almost anything — including literally selling ads promoting child pornography.

Is the French investigation against me political? It certainly fits the pattern we see elsewhere, mostly in authoritarian countries. And it definitely raises questions.

In time, this investigation may itself be investigated — especially now that Macron’s war against free speech is facing pushback. This month, France’s Constitutional Council struck down his social media ban for children under 15 on freedom-of-expression grounds.

In the end, freedom and truth will prevail ✊

📡 Pezeshkian urges stronger UN role in addressing international crises

📌 Tehran, IRNA – President Masoud Pezeshkian has called for a more effective and efficient role for the United Nations in dealing with international developments and crises, saying international institutions should not allow powerful states to act with impunity.

Pezeshkian made the remarks on Tuesday during a meeting with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit and the SCO Plus meeting in Kyrgyzstan.
​
Pezeshkian thanked Guterres for his positions condemning US-Israeli attacks against Iran, saying the attacks demonstrated a disregard for basic humanitarian principles and international law.
​
Pezeshkian said the recent agreement aimed at ending the war should be respected and its parties should remain committed to their obligations. He stressed that Iran did not seek war and considered conflict to be in the interest of no one.
​
The president, however, said Tehran would not accept the use of force or threats, adding that recognition of the rights of the Iranian people, a return to the agreement and implementation of US commitments were necessary to resolve the current situation.
​
He called on international organizations and institutions to play a more effective role in preventing certain countries from using their power and military capabilities to engage in aggression and commit crimes.
​
Guterres, for his part, said his approach during his tenure had focused on respect for the rule of law, peace and reducing conflicts, including during the recent war against Iran. He said his statements had consistently called for a peaceful and diplomatic solution to the conflict.
​
The UN chief believed Israel had drawn the United States into the war with Iran and had sought to weaken and destroy the West Asian country.
​
Guterres said he had been the only UN secretary-general to condemn the attack on Iran before the UN Security Council and the US representative, adding that the position had brought him considerable pressure and consequences.
​
Referring to the recent agreement aimed at ending the war, Guterres said the United Nations had welcomed its signing and viewed it as an important political achievement for Iran and a step toward ending the conflict, regretting that the agreement had faced challenges.
​
He expressed hope that the war would end as soon as possible
